findings.candidate_reasoning: snprintf returns the would-be length (not capped to sizeof(msg)) when truncating. If module->name is > ~1019 chars, name_len >= sizeof(msg). Then vsnprintf(msg + name_len, sizeof(msg) - name_len, ...) writes past msg[] since msg+name_len is past the buffer end, and sizeof(msg) - name_len underflows as size_t to a huge value.
findings.dataflow_summary: MODULE LOAD with long module name -> module->name -> snprintf returns name_len > sizeof(msg) -> vsnprintf(msg + name_len, sizeof(msg) - name_len, ...) writes OOB
findings.proof_source: module->name from loaded .so via REDISMODULE_INIT (attacker-controlled module name > 1019 chars)
findings.proof_sink: vsnprintf(msg + name_len, sizeof(msg) - name_len, fmt, ap) writes past end of char msg[1024]

stage_a_summary.candidate_reasoning: No bounds check on name_len before using as offset. Requires loading a module with name > 1019 chars. Requires MODULE LOAD privilege (admin + enable-module-command). Not remotely exploitable without auth.

evidence_synthesis.synthesis: Real buffer overflow in moduleLogRaw, but exploitation requires MODULE LOAD which already gives RCE — redundant.

ruling.reason: MODULE LOAD already provides arbitrary code execution via dlopen. A buffer overflow in moduleLogRaw during module logging adds no additional capability — the attacker already has full RCE from the loaded .so. Privilege tautology: the prerequisite (MODULE LOAD) already implies the outcome (code execution).

stage_f_summary.review_notes: Ruled out D-1.5. Correct — MODULE LOAD prerequisite already grants RCE.

findings.candidate_reasoning: CONFIG SET dir calls chdir(argv[0]) with no path validation. Combined with CONFIG SET dbfilename and BGSAVE, allows writing arbitrary RDB files to any writable path. Classic Redis RCE vector. Protected by enable-protected-configs (default OFF — blocks CONFIG SET dir). When misconfigured (enable-protected-configs=yes), any admin user can write files anywhere.
findings.dataflow_summary: CONFIG SET dir <path> -> chdir(argv[0]) at config.c:2741 -> BGSAVE -> rdbSaveToFile writes dump.rdb to new cwd
findings.proof_sink: chdir(argv[0]) at config.c:2741; rdbSaveBackground at rdb.c:4605

stage_a_summary.candidate_reasoning: Confirmed design-level write-anywhere. Blocked by default (PROTECTED_CONFIG + enable-protected-configs=no), but commonly misconfigured. Well-documented real-world Redis RCE vector.

evidence_synthesis.synthesis: Real write-anywhere primitive via CONFIG SET dir + BGSAVE. Blocked by default (enable-protected-configs=no), but exploitable when misconfigured. Well-documented real-world attack vector.

stage_f_summary.review_notes: CVSS 8.0 High. AC:H justified by enable-protected-configs default blocking CONFIG SET dir. PR:H correct for @admin ACL. Well-documented attack vector, no changes needed.

findings.candidate_reasoning: The Lua sandbox loads luaopen_os making the full os library available. os.execute in bundled Lua (deps/lua/src/loslib.c:38-41) calls system(). The readonly table protection only blocks writes to the table, not calls of existing C functions. os.execute is never explicitly removed. EVAL is @scripting ACL (not @admin), so any authenticated user with default ACL can execute shell commands.
findings.dataflow_summary: EVAL <lua_script> -> luaopen_os loaded (script_lua.c:1233) -> os.execute('cmd') -> system() in deps/lua/src/loslib.c:39
findings.proof_source: Attacker-controlled Lua script via EVAL command
findings.proof_sink: system() call in deps/lua/src/loslib.c:39 via os.execute

stage_a_summary.candidate_reasoning: os.execute calls system() and is loaded into the Lua sandbox but never removed. Readonly flag prevents table writes, not function calls. Any authenticated user with @scripting ACL can achieve RCE via EVAL.

issues: Verified: os_execute at deps/lua/src/loslib.c:38-41 calls system(). luaopen_os at script_lua.c:1233 loads it. Readonly at lvm.c:141 only checks SETTABLE. No removal of os.execute found in eval.c or script_lua.c.

evidence_synthesis.synthesis: os.execute loaded in Lua sandbox, never removed. Readonly table protection only prevents writes, not function calls (lvm.c:141). EVAL is @scripting not @admin — any authenticated user gets RCE via os.execute -> system().

stage_f_summary.review_notes: CVSS 8.8 High. Highest-impact confirmed finding. PR:L correct — EVAL is @scripting not @admin. Verified: os.execute loaded, never removed, readonly only prevents table writes. Code path: EVAL -> luaCreateFunction -> luaL_loadbuffer -> script calls os.execute -> system(). No corrections.

findings.candidate_reasoning: MODULE LOAD calls dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL) with no path sanitization beyond stat() execute-permission check. Attacker-controlled path goes directly to dlopen. Gated by enable-module-command (default: disabled). When enabled, trivial RCE by loading a malicious .so.
findings.dataflow_summary: MODULE LOAD <path> -> moduleLoad(c->argv[2]->ptr) -> dlopen(path) at module.c:13349

stage_a_summary.candidate_reasoning: No path sanitization. Direct dlopen of attacker-supplied path. Gated by enable-module-command (default: disabled) and CMD_ADMIN ACL.

evidence_synthesis.synthesis: MODULE LOAD works as designed — dlopen of admin-specified path is the feature, not a vulnerability.

ruling.reason: MODULE LOAD is explicitly designed to load arbitrary shared libraries for execution. The 'no path sanitization' is not a vulnerability — it is the intended behavior. An admin who can run MODULE LOAD is expected to load any .so. The capability IS the privilege.

stage_f_summary.review_notes: Ruled out D-1.5. Correct — MODULE LOAD is designed functionality, not a vulnerability.

findings.candidate_reasoning: Cluster bus accepts connections with no cryptographic auth — only 4-byte magic 'RCmb' and version check. Any network peer reaching the cluster port can inject MEET messages (join cluster unconditionally at line 2962), PUBLISH messages, or FAILOVER_AUTH_REQUEST. No signing or identity verification of messages.
findings.dataflow_summary: Network attacker -> cluster bus port -> clusterReadHandler -> clusterProcessPacket -> MEET: clusterAddNode / PUBLISH: pubsubPublishMessage / FAILOVER: clusterSendFailoverAuthIfNeeded
findings.proof_source: Any network connection to cluster bus port (client_port + 10000)

stage_a_summary.candidate_reasoning: Cluster bus has no authentication beyond 4-byte magic. Any on-path attacker can inject MEET, PUBLISH, or FAILOVER requests. Active in cluster mode by default.

issues: Verified: line 2945 if (!sender && type == CLUSTERMSG_TYPE_MEET) -> line 2958 createClusterNode -> line 2962 clusterAddNode. Unconditional for unknown senders.

evidence_synthesis.synthesis: Cluster bus accepts MEET/PUBLISH/FAILOVER with only 4-byte magic check. No crypto auth. Any network peer reaching bus port can join cluster, inject pub/sub, or influence failover.

preconditions: requires network access to cluster bus port (client_port + 10000)

stage_f_summary.review_notes: CVSS 9.6 Critical. AV:A confirmed — cluster bus is a separate port, typically requires same-network access. S:C confirmed — MEET injection affects all cluster nodes. No TLS or HMAC on cluster bus messages. No corrections.

findings.candidate_reasoning: masterauth defaults to NULL. Without it, replica does not send AUTH. If TLS not configured (default), replication is cleartext TCP. MITM can intercept handshake and inject crafted FULLRESYNC response with malicious RDB. Replica loads via rdbLoadRioWithLoadingCtx (replication.c:2518) with no integrity verification.
findings.dataflow_summary: MITM on replication port -> forge FULLRESYNC -> replica calls rdbLoadRioWithLoadingCtx with attacker-controlled RDB data
findings.proof_source: Network-level MITM on replication TCP stream (no auth, no TLS by default)

stage_a_summary.candidate_reasoning: masterauth=NULL by default, no TLS by default. Replication is cleartext unauthenticated. MITM can inject arbitrary RDB. Exploitability depends on RDB deserialization safety.

issues: Verified: line 3133 if (server.masterauth) — AUTH only sent when masterauth is set. Default is NULL.

evidence_synthesis.synthesis: Replication stream is cleartext with no auth by default. MITM can inject crafted RDB. Data integrity compromise confirmed. Memory corruption via RDB parser requires separate bugs.

preconditions: requires MITM position on replication network path

stage_f_summary.review_notes: CVSS 7.4 High. AC:H correct for MITM requirement. C:N appropriate — attacker can inject data but doesn't read existing data via this path alone. No corrections.

findings.candidate_reasoning: AUTH with username 'internal connection' and correct cluster secret sets c->user=NULL and c->authenticated=1. All ACL checks return ACL_OK when u==NULL. The cluster secret is transmitted in plaintext PING extension messages over the cluster bus. In non-TLS deployments, a passive network observer can sniff the secret and authenticate as unrestricted internal connection on the client port.
findings.dataflow_summary: Sniff cluster bus PING ext -> extract internal_secret -> AUTH 'internal connection' <secret> on client port -> c->user=NULL -> all ACL checks bypassed
findings.proof_source: AUTH 'internal connection' <sniffed_secret> from any network client
findings.proof_sink: c->user=NULL at acl.c:3241; ACL_OK at lines 1776, 1832, 1859

stage_a_summary.candidate_reasoning: Internal auth path accessible from client port. Cluster secret is strong (40 hex chars from /dev/urandom) but transmitted in plaintext PING extensions. Non-TLS cluster deployments are vulnerable to secret sniffing -> full ACL bypass.

issues: Verified: line 3241 c->user = NULL. Line 3238 c->authenticated = 1. Lines 3235 time_independent_strcmp with cluster secret.

evidence_synthesis.synthesis: Cluster secret transmitted in plaintext PING extensions. Sniffing it enables AUTH as 'internal connection' on client port, setting c->user=NULL which bypasses all ACL checks. Full privilege escalation from network observer to unrestricted access.

preconditions: requires passive sniffing on cluster bus network
TLS for cluster bus must be off

stage_f_summary.review_notes: CVSS 8.3 High. AV:A and AC:H correct — requires passive sniffing on cluster bus network segment (adjacent), which is a non-trivial precondition. S:C correct — bypasses ALL ACL, enabling full unrestricted access including CONFIG, MODULE, DEBUG if enabled. No corrections.

findings.function: run steps across ~20 jobs (test, sentinel tests, cluster tests)

issues: File not in C source inventory (YAML workflow file) but verified to exist at .github/workflows/daily.yml

evidence_synthesis.synthesis: Real shell injection in CI workflow, but requires write access which already implies ability to modify CI pipelines directly.

findings.proof_sink: actions/checkout@v4 repository: parameter -> subsequent make/runtest execution
